raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

`context_attention_fwd` in `prefix_prefill.py` runs `ROCM_ATTN`'s prefills and spec-decode verifies. It gets much slower when a long prefill shares a batch with short requests, which is the normal mixed step of chunked prefill. This PR fixes two causes:

1. **Grid order.** The grid was `(batch, head, query_block)`, with the batch on the fastest axis. MI300/MI355 deal workgroups round-robin over 8 XCDs. The programs of one request have linear ids `i, i + b, i + 2b, ...` for batch size `b`, so with even `b` they reach only some of the XCDs. Decodes (`query_len == 1`) return at once, so a prefill batched with decodes runs on part of the GPU. This PR uses `(head, query_block, batch)`, with the batch on the slowest axis.
2. **Empty query blocks.** Every request gets `cdiv(max_query_len, BLOCK_M)` query blocks. A 4-token verify batched with a 16k-token chunk gets 128 blocks. 127 of them have no rows but still loop over the whole context. They now return early.

Found while profiling `ROCM_ATTN` against `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` for #61433.

## Claims

- A prefill mixed with decodes or spec verifies runs as fast as the prefill alone. Before this PR it was up to 16× slower.
- The output is bit-identical to the current kernel.
- `ROCM_ATTN` end-to-end throughput rises up to 6.3× on Qwen3-8B (MI355X, 64k input, EAGLE3).
- Requests served one at a time do not change.

## Validation

**Kernel.** 8k-token chunk on a 16k prefix, Qwen3-8B shapes (32 query heads, 8 KV heads, head size 128, bf16, block size 16), MI355X, `triton.testing.do_bench`. The chunk is batched with `b - 1` decodes:

| b | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 | 12 | 16 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| main (ms) | 9.1 | 18.4 | 10.4 | 36.8 | 10.3 | 20.8 | 10.3 | 80.2 | 40.3 | 143.9 |

Each fix on its own:

| batch | main | grid order only | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| chunk alone | 9.1 ms | 9.1 ms | 9.1 ms |
| + 1 decode | 18.6 ms | 9.1 ms | 9.2 ms |
| + 7 decodes | 73.5 ms | 9.1 ms | 9.2 ms |
| + 7 verifies (q=2, kv 1k) | 73.7 ms | 12.2 ms | 9.2 ms |
| + 7 verifies (q=4, kv 32k) | 148.7 ms | 117.0 ms | 11.6 ms |

The output matches `main` exactly (max diff 0.0) on a batch of mixed query lengths (1, 3, 300, 1, 2000).

**Unit tests.** `tests/kernels/attention/test_prefix_prefill.py` gives the same results with and without this PR. On the nightly image I used, 41 cases fail on both sides, all with `TypeError: chunked_prefill_paged_decode() got an unexpected keyword argument 'use_interleaved_v_cache'` or `'types.SimpleNamespace' object has no attribute 'use_cascade'`. They come from the image's other modules being older than the tests, not from this kernel.

**End to end.** Qwen3-8B with YaRN ×4, `ROCM_ATTN` (the default), MRV2, 1024 output tokens with `--ignore-eos`, temperature 0, MI355X. Nightly `0.30.1rc1.dev558+g0cbac6cd1` with only `prefix_prefill.py` swapped. Without spec decode, decodes return at once, so only the grid order matters.

```
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B --max-model-len 131072 --max-num-seqs 256 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --hf-overrides '{"rope_scaling": {"rope_type": "yarn", "factor": 4.0, "original_max_position_embeddings": 32768}, "max_position_embeddings": 132096}' \
  [--speculative-config '{"method": "eagle3", "model": "RedHatAI/Qwen3-8B-speculator.eagle3", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}']
vllm bench serve --dataset-name custom --custom-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos --temperature 0 --max-concurrency C ...
```

Output tok/s:

| spec decode | input, concurrency | main | this PR | speedup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| none | 8k, 1 | 237.5 | 240.0 | 1.01× |
| none | 8k, 16 | 1052 | 1339 | 1.27× |
| none | 8k, 64 | 1357 | 1949 | 1.44× |
| none | 64k, 1 | 91.9 | 92.2 | 1.00× |
| none | 64k, 8 | 50.4 | 108.8 | 2.16× |
| none | 64k, 16 | 45.2 | 110.0 | 2.43× |
| EAGLE3 | 8k, 1 | 62.1 | 65.4 | 1.05× |
| EAGLE3 | 8k, 16 | 219 | 485 | 2.21× |
| EAGLE3 | 8k, 64 | 106 | 525 | 4.96× |
| EAGLE3 | 64k, 1 | 6.5 | 6.4 | 0.98× |
| EAGLE3 | 64k, 8 | 11.4 | 38.5 | 3.38× |
| EAGLE3 | 64k, 16 | 6.4 | 40.1 | 6.27× |

Acceptance length is the same on both sides (1.87–1.89 at 8k, 1.25–1.29 at 64k). Without spec decode at 64k, concurrency 8, p99 ITL drops from 3.3 s to 1.6 s. Over the sweep, the `main` server log has 50 intervals at 0 generation tok/s; with this PR it has none.

## Details

- Both kernels (`_fwd_kernel` and `_fwd_kernel_alibi`) read `cur_head`, `start_m` and `cur_batch` from program ids 0, 1 and 2, and both launches use the new grid order.
- The early return skips query blocks with no rows. Such a block loaded no queries and stored no output (both are masked by `offs_m < cur_batch_query_len`), so the output does not change.
- Not fixed here: a spec verify with `query_len` of 2–4 still takes a whole `BLOCK_M = 128` tile per query head. That makes `ROCM_ATTN`'s verify step 3–14× slower than `TRITON_ATTN`'s decode kernel. It needs a separate kernel change.
- Tests: no new test. The change only reorders the grid and skips query blocks that have no rows, The existing `test_prefix_prefill.py` cases already cover it for both kernels: they draw random query lengths per request, so shorter requests get query blocks with no rows. They run in the AMD `kernels/attention` CI step.

**Author review.** I have reviewed the code changes and this description by hand.

files.patch:
@@ -186,9 +186,10 @@ def _fwd_kernel(
     # sequence with query only (e.g. IQuest LoopCoder's `attn(q, None, None)`).
     KV_FROM_CACHE: tl.constexpr = False,
 ):
-    cur_batch = tl.program_id(0)
-    cur_head = tl.program_id(1)
-    start_m = tl.program_id(2)
+    # Heads vary fastest across programs (see context_attention_fwd).
+    cur_head = tl.program_id(0)
+    start_m = tl.program_id(1)
+    cur_batch = tl.program_id(2)
 
     cur_kv_head = cur_head // num_queries_per_kv
 
@@ -205,6 +206,11 @@ def _fwd_kernel(
     # generally, N goes over kv, while M goes over query_len
     block_start_loc = BLOCK_M * start_m
 
+    # Blocks past the end of a short query (e.g. a spec decode batched with a
+    # long prefill) have no rows to compute.
+    if block_start_loc >= cur_batch_query_len:
+        return
+
     # initialize offsets
     # [BLOCK_SIZE]; starts at 0
     offs_bs_n = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_SIZE)
@@ -565,9 +571,10 @@ def _fwd_kernel_alibi(
     INTERLEAVED_V_PACK_FACTOR: tl.constexpr,
 ):
     # attn_bias[]
-    cur_batch = tl.program_id(0)
-    cur_head = tl.program_id(1)
-    start_m = tl.program_id(2)
+    # Heads vary fastest across programs (see context_attention_fwd).
+    cur_head = tl.program_id(0)
+    start_m = tl.program_id(1)
+    cur_batch = tl.program_id(2)
 
     cur_kv_head = cur_head // num_queries_per_kv
 
@@ -585,6 +592,11 @@ def _fwd_kernel_alibi(
 
     block_start_loc = BLOCK_M * start_m
 
+    # Blocks past the end of a short query (e.g. a spec decode batched with a
+    # long prefill) have no rows to compute.
+    if block_start_loc >= cur_batch_query_len:
+        return
+
     # initialize offsets
     offs_n = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_N)
     offs_d = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_DMODEL_PADDED)
@@ -925,8 +937,8 @@ def context_attention_fwd(
         # due to increased use of GPU shared memory
         # if q.dtype is torch.float32:
         BLOCK = BASE_BLOCK // 2 if q_dtype_is_f32 else BASE_BLOCK
-        # batch, head,
-        grid = (batch, head, triton.cdiv(max_input_len, BLOCK))
+        # head, query block, batch
+        grid = (head, triton.cdiv(max_input_len, BLOCK), batch)
         _fwd_kernel_alibi[grid](
             q,
             k,
@@ -991,7 +1003,11 @@ def context_attention_fwd(
     BLOCK_N = 64
     TRITON_BLOCK_SIZE = 32
 
-    grid_fn = lambda META: (batch, head, triton.cdiv(max_input_len, META["BLOCK_M"]))
+    # Put the batch on the slowest grid axis. With it on the fastest one, all
+    # programs of a request share one residue of the linear program id, and on
+    # GPUs that deal workgroups round-robin across dies (MI300/MI355 XCDs) a
+    # long prefill mixed with decodes (which return at once) runs on one die.
+    grid_fn = lambda META: (head, triton.cdiv(max_input_len, META["BLOCK_M"]), batch)
     _fwd_kernel[grid_fn](
         q,
         k,
